object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A record of a compliance risk review performed on a vendor; a vendor accumulates review records over time, at most one being current and signed off.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask. It's not a checkbox on the vendor.
A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor's identifying legal entity vs duplicate records: tax ID is explicitly not unique due to duplicate onboarding and multi-entity parent groups, and there's an acknowledged unresolved cleanup project. Should the model account for a 'canonical entity' grouping of duplicate vendor records, or is this purely a data-quality issue out of scope?

source_references.excerpt: You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
The duplicates are a real problem. There's a cleanup project that's been on the roadmap for two years.

ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses: three distinct addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) are mentioned but not modeled in detail, and are noted as 'frequently different and frequently wrong.' Should each be a separate fact type/value type with its own structure (street, city, etc.), and are they optional or mandatory?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is overloaded between Procurement (spend tier: bronze/silver/gold) and Compliance (risk tier: low/medium/high). Although the model captures both as separate fields, the transcript notes ongoing terminology confusion in practice ('half the room hears different things'). Should the system/UI enforce distinct labels to prevent miscommunication, even though the data model is already correctly separated?

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: Post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (e.g., a 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a steering group / Legal decision. No constraint should be modeled for this until decided.

source_references.excerpt: Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off -- existing POs complete, no new ones can be raised.
This goes to the sourcing steering group. It's a policy call, not a modeling call ... what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Mei's informal spreadsheet tracks a 'preferred vendor' flag used when multiple vendors can supply the same item, but it's explicitly ad hoc with no defined criteria or process. Facilitator agreed not to model it, but this is a known gap that stakeholders may want formalized later. What would the criteria be if formalized?

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere.
I'm going to note that as a gap rather than a rule ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: The creation-time control for PurchaseOrder ('you can't raise one against a vendor who isn't active') was stated but not formally captured as a constraint pending clarity on the suspension/run-off resolution. Should a constraint be added that PurchaseOrder can only be raised against a Vendor with VendorStatus = active, or is this contingent on the unresolved suspension policy?

source_references.excerpt: Purchase orders. A PO is raised against exactly one vendor, and you can't raise one against a vendor who isn't active.

ambiguities.description: Contact identification scheme is not explicitly discussed (no contact ID or unique identifier mentioned in transcript); reference_mode 'contact_id' was inferred, not stated. Confirm how Contact records are actually identified in the system.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.

ambiguities.description: The vendor onboarding process describes six roughly parallel activities (record creation, tax documentation, banking details/verification, payment system entry, compliance review, approval based on spend) but only some of these (record, review, tax ID) were modeled in detail. Banking details, payment system entry, and spend-based approval were mentioned but never elaborated into fact types -- are these in scope for a fuller model?

source_references.excerpt: We create the record. We get their tax documentation. We get banking details, which goes through a separate verification because of the fraud thing last year. We get them into the payment system, which is a different system, which is part of why this is painful. Compliance does their piece. And then somebody has to actually approve it, which depends on how much we're planning to spend.
